title: Testing the language-symmetry account of representation geometry

original_idea.body: Testing the language-symmetry account of representation geometry (Karkada et al. 2026). Construct synthetic corpora with controlled symmetries, embed with a frozen small model, measure whether predicted geometry tracks input symmetry.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Bears on whether interpretability rests on real concepts, but the chain to catastrophic risk is indirect with skipped steps.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Synthetic corpora + frozen embedding + geometry metric; some conceptual depth but guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused symmetric-vs-asymmetric geometry comparison; designing corpora and metric adds effort.

low_compute.reasoning: Frozen small-model embeddings on synthetic corpora; near-CPU feasible.

novelty.reasoning: Independent probe of a very recent claim; angle plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Recent claim; independent empirical probe may be open.
